correctness.rationale: For admissible A(r,s) with 2r^2<=1+s, -1<=s<=1 and A≠11^T, direct centered-row Pearson correlation gives P(A)=Gamma(Q), Q=(2r-1-s)/sqrt((2r-1-s)^2+3(1-s)^2), Gamma(q)=A(q,2q^2-1). Every subsequent iterate is q↦f(q)=q/sqrt(4q^2+6q+3). Its monotone sign and fixed-point structure on q∈[-1,1] give q→-1 for r<s, q=-1/2 exactly when r=s (one-step equicorrelation), q→0 for r>s, including semidefinite endpoints. Taylor expansion at -1 gives quadratic coefficient 3/2 and derivative at 0 gives 1/sqrt3. Independently recomputed six admissible first Pearson row-correlations and the Gamma shape directly from centered row Gram products; full all-input proof is from the exact algebra and scalar inequalities, not sampling. Main claim is mathematically correct as stated.
